mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 5% for two consecutive months reduces discount rates, lowering the present value of future equity cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS excess over 5% (p > 0.05 in out-of-sample test).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +0.3% in a month following a rate hike, the expectation of future inflation increases, prompting investors to demand higher equity compensation and pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL change > +0.3% in month after FEDFUNDS hike
failure_condition: In 20-day windows after such CPIAUCSL spikes, SPX 20-day returns are not significantly higher than the 20-day mean of the prior 12 months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in PAYEMS (labor market tightness) above 8.5% in a month coincides with increased hiring momentum, which lowers real wage growth and reduces equity risk premia, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: During 5-day windows after such PAYEMS spikes, SPX 5-day returns show no negative relationship with the trigger (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When both GDPC1 (GDP) and HOUST (retail sales) grow simultaneously at a double-digit annualized rate for two consecutive quarters, it signals a late-cycle acceleration in consumer and business demand, which elevates S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > +10% AND HOUST growth > +10% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: In 20-day windows following such dual-high growth quarters, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically higher than the 20-day mean of the prior 6 months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of more than 2% for three months indicates weakening manufacturing capacity, which raises supply-side uncertainty and drives S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During 60-day windows after such declines, SPX 60-day returns show no significant negative relationship with INDPRO decline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4% for two consecutive months, it suggests strengthening labor market absorption, reducing wage growth pressures and lowering equity risk premia, which tends to produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In 20-day windows after such UNRATE declines, SPX 20-day returns are not significantly higher than the 20-day mean of the prior 12 months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in FEDFUNDS below 4% following a period of steady increases creates a policy divergence from the Fed's historical pattern, which increases market uncertainty and is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 4% after a streak of monthly increases
failure_condition: During 5-day windows after such a drop, SPX 5-day returns show no negative relationship with the trigger (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous rise of both RSAFS (retail sales) and GDPC1 (GDP) by more than 5% in the same month indicates accelerated demand across sectors, which elevates growth expectations and pushes S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > +5% AND GDPC1 > +5% in the same month
failure_condition: In 20-day windows after such dual-high months, SPX 20-day returns are not significantly higher than the 20-day mean of the prior 18 months (p > 0.05).
